vehicle_classes.A: Light vehicle — height <= 2.8 m AND length <= 12.5 m (cars, motorcycles, small vans). Towing or roof load that breaches either dimension reclassifies to B.

notes: Prices are the published 1 July 2026 quarterly schedule unless a different effective_date is stated on the road (WestConnex: 1 January 2026, its own annual cycle).
Non-WestConnex Sydney motorways are indexed QUARTERLY (1 Jan / 1 Apr / 1 Jul / 1 Oct). WestConnex roads are indexed ANNUALLY on 1 January. Your ingest job must re-scrape on both cadences.
Do not hardcode these values in application code. Load from this file, version it, and treat a stale effective_date as a monitoring alert.
Authoritative per-trip pricing is the TfNSW Toll Calculator API v2. This file is the fallback / cross-check / offline table.
Records with confidence != "verified" MUST be confirmed before production use.

2026-09-07 CORRECTION PASS: every price below was re-verified against nsw.gov.au and the relevant Linkt toll-pricing pages on that date (see each entry's own source_url/retrieved_at). Two real defects were fixed — Westlink M7's $/km rate was previously DERIVED from a self-measured gantry corridor instead of Linkt's published $0.5252/km; WestConnex (M4/M8/M5E/M4M5 Link) was previously confidence='not_captured' with every price NULL and is now priced from Linkt's published flagfall+per-km formula and per-road/network caps. A modelling defect was also fixed: 'Military Road E-Ramp' was previously seeded as its own TollRoad; it is a toll POINT of Lane Cove Tunnel, not a separate road, and is now modelled as one. A second modelling defect was fixed: the old 'M4M5_ROZELLE' road conflated two DIFFERENT Linkt-named segments (the priced 'M4-M8 Link' and the unpriced 'Rozelle Interchange') under one id because they share physical gantry infrastructure in the source gantry CSV; they are now two separate roads, split by gantry location (Haberfield/St Peters = M4-M8 Link; Anzac Bridge/Iron Cove Bridge/City West Link = Rozelle Interchange) — see scripts/seed_toll_roads.py for the full reasoning, flagged there as an interpretation call since the source data itself does not label individual gantries by segment name.
See app.models.toll's module docstring for the once_per_road / cumulative_per_point / distance_metered charging_policy field this pass introduced, and app.services.tolls for how it's applied.

Neither source states these are cumulative, and they are a main-carriageway/alternate-ramp pair a real vehicle uses ONE of — modelled once_per_road: whichever point is actually crossed first sets the (real, per-point) price; a second, different point of the same road later in the same trip is not charged again.
